findings.impact: With a configured token (and optionally AUTO_UPLOAD=1) the toolkit pushes the untouched results tree - hostname, serials, MAC/IP inventory, telemetry and logs - to whatever GITHUB_REPO/GITHUB_BRANCH are set, with no per-upload confirmation, no redaction, and no field minimization. Combined with the documented default repo (recorded as PUBLIC by the repo's own prior audit GOV-P3-001), identifiers are published to a world-readable location automatically, which is difficult to reverse and easy to trigger accidentally.
findings.recommendation: Make publication an explicit, confirmed action (never silent auto-upload), run a mandatory redaction/minimization pass before any upload, require a private destination by default, show the exact file/field set being published, and document consent/retention for uploaded data.

findings.impact: The control-plane database accumulates runner IP addresses, hostnames, persistent machine identifiers, telemetry, logs and artifacts indefinitely. There is no documented retention window, no automatic pruning, and no purge job, so personal/device data outlives its purpose and grows without bound - a data-minimization and retention-expectation gap for a tool that explicitly says the db should never be committed.
findings.recommendation: Define and document a retention policy (e.g. keep telemetry for N days, purge logs/artifacts after M) and implement a scheduled prune; document that addr is a client IP and consider not persisting it (or hashing it) unless needed; add a purge/export command for operator data-subject requests.

findings.title: No privacy/analytics governance artifacts (vendor list, consent, do-not-track, retention docs) and no privacy tests
evidence: grep for privacy|consent|gdpr|ccpa|do not track|opt-in|opt-out|cookie across docs/ returns only prior-audit text and unrelated 'opt-in' wording - no privacy policy, vendor list or retention doc exists
docs/ contains only CONTROL_PLANE.md, DATA.md, FUTURE_WORK.md, METHODOLOGY.md, PHASE_TIMINGS.md and the prior audit run - no privacy/analytics document
No analytics/tracking/consent tests exist: tests/ covers reporting, control plane, packaging and updates only; grep for redact|anonym|pii in tests/ returns nothing

Third-party endpoints contacted by the toolkit are functional only (bench/Invoke-NetBench.ps1:37,58 and bench/net_bench.py:95,97 speed.cloudflare.com; bench/upload.py:31 api.github.com; bench/bootstrap.py:48 python-build-standalone; bench/Get-Sensors.ps1:17 LibreHardwareMonitor; bench/Install-GpuFanCurve.ps1:34 nvfancontrol) but are not inventoried anywhere
findings.impact: Operators and future agents have no single place that lists which identifiers are collected, where they are sent, for how long they are kept, or how a user opts out - and no test guards redaction/consent behavior, so privacy controls can regress silently. The web dashboard itself (server/web/app.js) has no analytics, no cookies and only a local app.js script, so end-user web-tracking concerns are genuinely not applicable, but the machine-inventory/privacy surface remains undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/PRIVACY.md (data inventory: fields, purpose, storage, retention, third-party endpoints, opt-out) and a vendor/endpoint list; document consent for upload; add a unit test asserting the redaction mode strips serials/MAC/IP and that no shareable path emits identifiers without redaction.
